aim: Expose cold instrument, cold hands, fast pulse, accelerating music, anxiety. Surplus allowed as exploratory material.

text: The piano had been brought in from the loading bay and was cold. The room was cold, and the keys were cold. Clara's hands were cold on the keys. Her heart was beating fast; she was frightened and played faster and faster. The judges were sitting beyond the lights. There was a rest coming in the score, and she didn't want to stop.
notes: Deliberate overexplicit draft; not asserted as a model-generated sample.

observed.finding: coldness appears on room, piano, keys and hands

observed.witness: heart was beating fast / played faster and faster
observed.finding: acceleration shared between bodily and musical event

observed.witness: rest coming ... didn't want to stop
observed.finding: musical pause can become future dramatic pressure

uncertainties: A redundant style could be desired in another regime.

text:
The porter had left the fire door open. Clara rested her fingers on the keys, then lifted them. Beyond the lights the judges waited.

She began. Her hands raced cold across the keys. The piano beating faster and faster beneath them.

Two bars of rest at the foot of the page. She took neither.

observed.finding: weak physical cue compatible with cold contact, not proof

observed.witness: Two bars of rest / She took neither
observed.finding: new performance event; changes story and may be compelling or overly neat

uncertainties: May be opaque to a reader unfamiliar with score notation.
